document: P09 rule and project decision matrix

revision_history.note: Initial decision-support draft (original inventory date, kept for history).

Second research pass upgraded the exchange, swallow/respawn and PVP-item evidence to claims C1-C22; later the same day the user decided (a)-(d) (proportional shrink, minimum conversion size, 60 s rotation, result-bonus layer), recorded in Docs/OPEN_DECISIONS.md and backfilled here. The four second-pass research sources now use the research sub-ids S-KB01-S-KB04 (they previously carried global-registry-style ids that collided with Docs/08_SOURCES_AND_OPEN_QUESTIONS.md); this file therefore matches that registry and Docs/Research/ReferenceRules/rules_matrix.md.

status: decision-support draft; 2026-11-14 user decisions (a)-(d) backfilled; original-game unknowns remain unknown
evidence_policy: Separate official published text, producer-interview statements and hands-on player reports from unknown original-game rules, project direction, provisional parameters, and actual implementation evidence. No gameplay was run or measured for this document. 2026-11-14 update: exchange, swallow/respawn and PVP-item rows upgraded from unknown to confirmed on the second research pass recorded in Docs/Research/KatamariBallRules/README.md (claims C1-C22); no number became an original-game value that the research does not state.

sources.access_and_limit: As recorded in T01 rules_matrix.md: full text fetched on 2026-10-10 UTC (2026-10-11 Asia/Shanghai). FAQ says KatamariBall is playable with friends, up to four per room, and lists Magnet/timer/rocket with platform activation controls. It does not establish detailed PVP interactions.

As recorded in T01 rules_matrix.md: full text fetched on 2026-10-10 UTC (2026-10-11 Asia/Shanghai). Announcement describes KatamariBall as a four-player battle mode: grow the ball within a time limit, exchange it for points, highest score wins. It does not specify transaction, KO, respawn, or item-in-PVP rules.

4Gamer interview with producer Ryo Ishida (Ishida Ryou), published 2025-09-20 after the 2025-09-05 media hands-on; quoted excerpts in Docs/Research/KatamariBallRules/sources/4gamer.net_producer-interview-2025-09-20.md. Establishes scoring requires placing the ball in the in-world conversion area, that exchange shrinks the ball, and that a swallowed player reappears elsewhere. It gives no match length, round count, conversion ratio, item list or map detail.

Japanese player report published 2025-10-29 (five days after release, PS5); excerpts in Docs/Research/KatamariBallRules/sources/note.com_player-report-sports-katamari.md. Adds the conversion area's location under the prince ship, its roughly 60-second relocation with a navigation icon, the minimum-size rejection, the size-banded collision outcomes, treasure-chest items, Brother bonus, and the three-category +50 pt result bonus. It gives no match length, round count, conversion ratio or respawn protection.

Katamaripedia versus-mode page last edited 2025-10-22; excerpt in Docs/Research/KatamariBallRules/sources/katamaripedia.miraheze.org_versus-mode.md. Cross-confirms deposit-at-S.S.-Prince, 60-second relocation, shrinking on deposit, respawn instead of elimination, and 'most points at the end of the match'. No footnotes; treated as Tier 3 corroboration only.

CGMagazine review; excerpt in Docs/Research/KatamariBallRules/sources/cgmagonline.com_review.md. Media-side wording that objects attached to the Katamari must be dropped off at designated goals. It does not explain scoring formula, shrinking, respawn or bonus points.

sources.limit: Project direction/prototypes, not evidence of original-game rules or implementation.

decisions.unit: players_per_match; duration unknown seconds; original result-bonus categories unknown (project default categories are PROVISIONAL)
official_confirmed: KatamariBall is described as a four-player battle mode.
Players grow a Katamari within a time limit and exchange it for points; highest score wins.
Tier-2 player report: at the result screen three categories each award +50 pt to that category's first place, and this can still change the ranking (S-KB02, claims C11-C12).
Tier-3 wiki states the goal is 'the most points at the end of the match' (S-KB03, claim C10, strongly implied only).
Rank/段位 rises only with first place and unlocks ball colours; it is explicitly not skill-based matchmaking (S-KB01, claim C17).
unknown: Exact match duration (no source gives it; only a 'remaining 1 minute' countdown appears), number of rounds/sets, tie handling, and how a deposit that arrives exactly at the cutoff is decided.

Original: which three of the five observed bonus categories are used per match, and whether they are fixed or rotating; the project's default three categories are a PROVISIONAL project choice, not an original rule.
Whether any online context fills the fourth slot with CPU.
project_decision_or_prototype: PCVR + Desktop first release; Quest excluded.
Project scope suggests 2–4 human players and has a provisional 180-second single-round prototype; neither is an original-game measurement.

Project adopts the original's second scoring layer on top of banked-score ranking: three categories each award +50 pt to that category's first place (Tier-2 evidence C11-C12; user decision 2026-11-14, Docs/OPEN_DECISIONS.md (d)). Banking remains the only primary scoring channel. The project default categories are swallowed opponents / max ball size / items absorbed, with ties awarding nothing; the category set and any weight are PROVISIONAL and must be announced to players.

decisions.decision_owner: user_and_lead; implementation parameters after relevant playtest
decisions.do_not_claim: Do not state that 180 seconds or the project's 2–4 participation reproduces the original rules, and do not present the project's bonus category set or weight as the original's. The original match length, round count and per-match bonus category set are still unknown.

decisions.unit: points; ball size traded for points; original conversion ratio and minimum size unknown; project uses residual 0.25 and a minimum diameter of 0.55 m (PROVISIONAL)
official_confirmed: Scoring is not automatic and not continuous: the ball must be physically brought into an in-world conversion area, producer quote 'ポイントを得るには塊を「変換エリア」に入れなければいけません' (S-KB01, claim C1).
Exchange trades ball size for points and the ball shrinks: '変換エリアでは塊が小さくなるのと引き換えにポイントを獲得' (S-KB01, claim C2). It is not reset to the initial ball.
Shrinking has a real cost: with a smaller ball you can no longer roll up large objects (S-KB01, claim C5).

The conversion area sits directly under the prince ship (S.S. Prince) and relocates about every 60 seconds, shown by a navigation icon (S-KB02 + S-KB03, claim C3, strongly implied: Tier 2 plus Tier 3, not a Tier-1 statement).
A ball that is too small scores nothing: '小さい塊の場合は、ポイントをゲット出来ません' (S-KB02, claim C4).
Media wording agrees that the ball must be delivered to designated goals (S-KB04).
unknown: Original conversion formula/ratio, whether it is banded or capped, and the original's numeric minimum conversion size (the project's 0.25 residual and 0.55 m minimum are PROVISIONAL project values).
Trigger radius, animation, service time, whether an exchange can be interrupted, and how long before a relocation it is announced.
Ordering when a conversion request and the match cutoff land on the same tick.
project_decision_or_prototype: Project uses unbanked risk growth and confirmed banked score as distinct ledgers; score ranking uses confirmed banked points.

Project keeps a rotating in-world banking anchor with a pre-announcement, which is structurally the same shape as the original (C3); the period is 60 s (aligned with the original's strongly implied ~60 s), with four fixed anchors activated at 0/60/120/180 s in the 180 s prototype, so only three 60 s windows are used and the fourth anchor activates at the final whistle; the next match starts one anchor later so no anchor stays idle (PROVISIONAL layout value; user decision 2026-11-14, Docs/OPEN_DECISIONS.md (c)).

Project banking shrinks the ball instead of resetting it, in diameter space: post = max(start, start + (pre - start) * residual) with residual = 0.25, and a ball smaller than 0.55 m diameter cannot convert at all. Both numbers and the formula are PROJECT PROVISIONAL values (user decision 2026-11-14, Docs/OPEN_DECISIONS.md (a)/(b)); the original only confirms that exchange shrinks the ball (C2) and that a too-small ball scores nothing (C4), without publishing either value.

candidates.option: SELECTED - project explicit banking zone and transaction (with the 2026-11-14 shrink rule)
candidates.description: Use the current project contract: request/confirmation, idempotency, state change only on confirmed transaction, and a shrink instead of a reset. The manual, mid-match, repeatable in-world delivery is corroborated by S-KB01/S-KB02.
candidates.reject_basis_if_not_selected: It is still a project contract (single arbiter, idempotency, shrink formula) whose details go beyond what public sources state.

candidates.option: SELECTED - banking shrinks the ball by a residual fraction instead of resetting it, with a minimum conversion size (2026-11-14 user decision)
candidates.description: post = max(start, start + (pre - start) * residual) in diameter space with residual = 0.25; a ball below 0.55 m diameter is rejected. Both values and the formula are project PROVISIONAL values (Docs/OPEN_DECISIONS.md (a)/(b)); the original only confirms shrinking (C2) and a minimum-size rejection (C4).
candidates.reject_basis_if_not_selected: The ratio is a project invention, so pacing/fairness playtests must revisit it; 0.20 is closer to a reset and 0.30 makes the late game harder.

candidates.description: Previously an open candidate; excluded as the main channel because the producer states points come only from physically entering the conversion area (C1).
candidates.reject_basis_if_not_selected: Recording it as available would contradict the Tier-1 evidence, so it is kept only as an explicitly excluded alternative.

candidates.description: Previously an open candidate; excluded because points are produced only by the conversion act, not by rolling or by size alone (C1/C16).
candidates.reject_basis_if_not_selected: Recording it as available would contradict the Tier-1 evidence, so it is kept only as an explicitly excluded alternative.

candidates.option: Alternative exchange flow after project tests
candidates.description: Compare multiple simultaneous exchange points or a different announce lead time only through a scoped project decision.
candidates.reject_basis_if_not_selected: Would change map, UI, transaction, and fairness requirements.

decisions.do_not_claim: Do not claim the original resets the ball to its initial size (C20 is unconfirmed/contradicted), gives a conversion ratio or minimum-size value, or relocates the area exactly every 60 seconds as a Tier-1 fact. Do not present the project's residual 0.25, 0.55 m minimum, 60 s period or four-anchor rotation as original-game values.

decisions.unit: collision/size ratio dimensionless; threshold, contact radius and freeze duration unknown
official_confirmed: Swallowing exists: a larger opposing ball swallows yours on contact (S-KB01 'ほかのプレイヤーの塊が大きければ，ぶつかったときに巻き込まれることになるでしょう', claims C6/C8).
Same-size balls bounce off each other (S-KB02, claim C9).
Swallowing a smaller opponent interferes with that player; the smaller one is the victim (S-KB02, claims C6/C8).
A swallowed player is briefly immobilised and moved elsewhere; there is no elimination (S-KB01, claim C6).
unknown: The size ratio or absolute size difference that permits a swallow, any absolute immunity for small balls, contact direction and effective radius, freeze duration, simultaneous-contact resolution, and whether the swallower gains resources.
project_decision_or_prototype: Project retains swallow/KO and respawn as a project direction. The 1.35 size ratio in game design is a project prototype assumption only.

candidates.description: Use a parameter only after owner approval and deterministic authority tests.
candidates.reject_basis_if_not_selected: Leaves balance open and requires tuning evidence.

candidates.description: Select from multiplayer playtest data.
candidates.reject_basis_if_not_selected: No such data currently exists.

candidates.description: Gate the feature off in a test build if required evidence is absent.
candidates.reject_basis_if_not_selected: Would reduce the planned PVP feature set and alter test goals.

decisions.decision_owner: lead_for_project_rules; user_for_scope; T27/T39 testers for evidence
decisions.do_not_claim: 1.35 is neither original-game data nor a measured project balance value. The original's contact rules and freeze duration are not established.

decisions.unit: time in seconds unknown; documented score effect none
official_confirmed: Being swallowed is not elimination: '新たな場所に再出現するので大丈夫です' (the player reappears elsewhere), with a short period of not being able to move (S-KB01, claim C6).
No source states a score or resource loss for the swallowed player, so 'no loss of already-scored points' is strongly implied only (S-KB01, claim C7).
The review word 'battle royale' is a metaphor, not an official mode definition; elimination/ shrinking-zone readings are contradicted (claim C22).
unknown: Respawn wait duration (the source only says 'ちょっとのあいだ' — a very short while, no seconds), spawn selection, any spawn protection and its length, whether the victim spectates, and carried item/growth state after respawn.
project_decision_or_prototype: Project direction includes KO and respawn. Example values such as about 3 seconds wait and about 2 seconds protection are unvalidated project prototype numbers, not original rules.
Project adds elimination-time resource clearing and spawn protection that the original does not document; both are project choices, heavier than the confirmed original.

candidates.option: Configurable short KO and safe respawn
candidates.description: Preserve participant status, clear input, respawn at a safe point, test low-tier supply.
candidates.reject_basis_if_not_selected: Timing, safety, and resource availability remain unvalidated.

candidates.description: Select only after multiplayer and comfort/fairness tests.
candidates.reject_basis_if_not_selected: Long or short values may create farming, snowball, or downtime.

candidates.option: No respawn in a particular test mode
candidates.description: Use only as an explicitly scoped experiment, not silently as final design.
candidates.reject_basis_if_not_selected: Conflicts with current project direction and changes match dynamics.

candidates.option: Mirror the original more closely: brief freeze, immediate reappear, no extra penalty
candidates.description: Drop the project's longer elimination and unbanked-resource clearing in favour of the confirmed original shape.
candidates.reject_basis_if_not_selected: Reduces the punishment for losing a fight and changes the risk model the project currently balances around.

decisions.decision_owner: lead_for_project_contract; T27/T39 human testers; user for scope
decisions.do_not_claim: The original has no elimination and documents no score loss, but its wait time, spawn choice and protection are unknown; do not present 3 s/2 s as original values.

decisions.unit: items; count, duration and effect values not established
official_confirmed: KatamariBall does deploy items: a rainbow treasure chest ('王様トレジャー') grants ordinary support items from the solo stages plus mode-specific items (S-KB02, claim C13).
The effect space is only two kinds: make your own ball bigger, or hinder opponents (S-KB02, claim C13).
A 'Brother' ('ブラザー') orbits your ball with a scoring bonus and disappears if an opponent rolls it up (S-KB02, claim C14).
Magnet and rocket being usable in the mode is strongly implied only ('いつものステージで使うサポートアイテムの他', claim C15); no PVP parameters are confirmed.
unknown: Full PVP item list and their values, spawn points, slot count, durations, whether items survive respawn or banking, chest refresh rules, and the exact mode-specific item roster.
project_decision_or_prototype: Project chose a single slot with Magnet and Rocket; Jump rising edge is the project input direction. This is not a claim of original PVP item rules.
Project does not implement the Brother bonus or the timer item.

candidates.description: Implement only after project-specific transaction and platform input gates. Direction is consistent with the confirmed existence of PVP support items.
candidates.reject_basis_if_not_selected: Selected subset; may require balancing and platform testing.

No one-map release choice, fairness threshold, original rule, commercial SKU, price, or public interface has been approved by this document; the only 2026-11-14 approvals recorded are the four rule decisions summarized in Docs/OPEN_DECISIONS.md.
No Unity, game, VR, multiplayer, commerce, or original-game playtest was performed.

On 2026-11-14 the user decided (a)-(d) - proportional shrink, minimum conversion size, 60 s rotation and the result-bonus layer - recorded in Docs/OPEN_DECISIONS.md and backfilled into this file the same day. Those four values are PROVISIONAL project values, not original-game values, and the remaining project values (180 s, 1.35, 3 s, 2 s) stay provisional too.
